draft.title: Health literacy
card: Health literacy is the set of skills a person uses to find, understand, judge and use health information. The aim is to make good decisions about health.
Find and understand
knowing where to look for information, such as a doctor, pharmacist or health department website, and being able to follow what it says.
Judge
checking whether information can be trusted. Ask who wrote it, whether it is based on evidence, and whether it is out of date or trying to sell something.
Use

acting on the information, such as following the directions on a medicine label or choosing when to see a doctor. A person who finds good information but does not use it is not using the full set of skills.
draft.remember: Health literacy is four skills in a chain: find, understand, judge and use.

a.q: Which person is showing health literacy?
opts: Sam checks who wrote an article on sleep before trusting it
Sam shares a health post because many people have liked it
Sam avoids reading any health advice so he is not confused
Sam follows the first diet tip he sees in a video
a.why: Sam is judging the information by checking who wrote it, which is one of the skills in health literacy. Sharing a post because it is popular is tempting, but likes do not show that information is based on evidence.
a.clue: Which choice checks whether information can be trusted?

b.q: Priya finds a clear website from a health department about vaccines and understands it. She then ignores the advice about when to get her booster. Which part of health literacy is she missing?
opts: Using the information to make a decision
Finding information from a reliable source
Understanding the words in the information
Judging who wrote the information
b.why: Priya found the website and understood it, so those skills are present. She did not act on the advice, so she is missing the use of information. Judging is the tempting option, but nothing in the case suggests she doubted the source.
b.clue: Look at what Priya did and did not do after reading.

a.best: Sam checks who wrote an article on sleep before trusting it

b.best: Using the information to make a decision

problems.detail: The remember line calls health literacy 'four skills in a chain', which suggests a strict order. The card only calls it a 'set of skills' and groups find and understand together under one heading, so the remember line sorts the ideas more neatly than the card does.
The clue 'Which choice checks whether information can be trusted?' points straight at the only option about checking information, so students can match the words without understanding the idea.

check.summary: The facts and both answers are sound. The remember line's 'four skills in a chain' imposes a tidier order than the card gives, and the clue for question a all but names the answer.
